content.overview: Article 36 provides that in Part IV (Directive Principles of State Policy), unless the context otherwise requires, ‘the State’ has the same meaning as in Part III. Thus the definition of State in Article 12 applies to the Directive Principles as well.
content.glance: For Part IV, ‘the State’ has the same meaning as in Part III (Article 12).
content.study:
Article 36 is a definitional bridge: the Article 12 meaning of ‘State’ (Union and State governments and legislatures, local authorities, and other authorities under the control of the Government of India) applies throughout Part IV unless context otherwise requires.

Directive Principles are addressed to the State in this expanded sense. They are not enforceable by any court (Article 37) but are fundamental in the governance of the country, and it is the duty of the State to apply them in making laws.

Examination: same meaning as Part III; link Arts 12 and 37; non-justiciable but fundamental in governance.

sections.heading: Key rule
sections.body: In Part IV, unless the context otherwise requires, ‘the State’ has the same meaning as in Part III.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does Article 36 provide?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 36 provides that in Part IV, unless the context otherwise requires, ‘the State’ has the same meaning as in Part III. The Article 12 definition of State therefore applies to the Directive Principles of State Policy.

examTips: State in Part IV = State in Part III (Art 12).
